claims.claim: Maricopa County heat-related deaths, 2025
claims.caveat: This is NOT a worker figure. It is a general-population count. Maricopa County does not record occupation: the MCDPH report carries no occupation, industry or work-relatedness variable anywhere in it, including the appendix tables (impact-evidence.md#1.17). Any claim that these are worker deaths is unsupported by the source.

claims.claim: Share of 2025 Maricopa County heat-related deaths that occurred on days NWS HeatRisk was not Major or Extreme (MCDPH Table F)
claims.source_title: MCDPH 2025 Heat-Related Deaths Report, Table F
claims.caveat: This is NOT a worker figure. It is a general-population count, and Maricopa County does not record occupation (impact-evidence.md#1.17), so this is not a statement that 64% of worker heat deaths fell on unflagged days. What it measures is how well the alert layer discriminates — a property of the alert, not of the decedents — and it is the same alert layer a supervisor reads each morning.

Contractor use of mobile heat safety apps (OSHA-NIOSH, AIHA) fell between the 2023 and 2025 waves — the trend is away from tooling, not toward it
claims.quote: 4 out of 5 options examined in 2023 declined a little in overall use in 2025: weather forecasts (95% to 87%)… mobile heat safety apps (35% to 22%). Only wet bulb globe temperature use remained the same at 13%.

claims.claim: Kwest Group testimony to OSHA: the operative signal employers act on is deviation from the local normal heat index, not an absolute threshold. The Construction Industry Safety Coalition then formalised the same basis in its post-hearing brief, citing the urban heat island effect by name
claims.value: not a prescriptive heat index number, but more of the change
claims.source_title: Stephen Kinn, Kwest Group / AGC — OSHA informal public hearing, docket OSHA-2021-0009, Day 3, pp. 15–16, 18 Jun 2025
claims.quote: The major concentration shouldn't be a prescriptive heat index number, but more of the change — going from what is a normal heat index in that location to what is a significant change or deviation from what that normal heat index is in that location. That's when we start seeing our problems on our projects. And that's where we really concentrate and get notice out to our guys… So it's not a uniform, one-size-fits-all. It's look at each location and what's significantly different.
